description.narrative: The objectives of this contributions are: 1) Develop evidence of high quality to deepen knowledge of poverty reduction. 2) Share evidence strategically to influence decisions. 3) Equip decision makers with evidence to improve living conditions for people living in poverty.

Denna insats ett kärnstöd som bidrar till IPA:s 2025 Strategic Ambitions - organisationens strategiplan för de kommande åren. Insatsen omfattar 40 MSEK under tre år, där aktivitetsperioden är mellan 2023 - 2025. Detta stöd fram har beretts inom ramen för Strategin för kapacitetsutveckling, partnerskap och metoder som stöder Agenda 2030 för hållbar utveckling (KAPAME). Målen med insatsen är: 1) Skapa evidens av hög kvalitet – för att fördjupa kunskapen om fattigdomsminkning. 2) Dela evidens strategiskt – för att påverka beslut. 3) Utrusta beslutsfattare evidens – för att förbättra villkoren för människor som lever i fattigdom.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement between The Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency, Sida and Innovations for Poverty Action regarding Core Support
Beslut om stöd till Innovations for Poverty Action 2022-2025

description.narrative:
IPA is describing a multitude of research projects, results and collaborations in the 20 countries they operate, in Asia, Africa and Latin America. Most of the research projects are ongoing and results are tentative.
Embedded Labs: IPA is currently collaborating with Ministries of Education in five countries to establish Embedded Evidence Labs, among them Rwanda, Kenya and Uganda. The primary objective is to enhance the use of data and evidence for education policy by embedding teams within the ministries. This approach can support a horizontal learning process, enabling both parties to learn from each other while simultaneously developing capacity in data and evidence utilization, in order to ultimately lead to improved learning outcomes for students and making a lasting impact on education policy
In Tanzania IPA is leading two research initiatives that aim to foster financial inclusion and encourage the adoption of mobile money. The first is the Transaction Cost Index, its goal is to establish the first ever index of the actual cost of completing mobile money transactions in Tanzania (as well as Uganda and Bangladesh). This index will encompass listed prices, unofficial fees like off the books agent charges, and non pecuniary costs such as failed transactions. The second initiative is the Interoperable Payments Systems. This research aims to explore the impact of interoperable payment systems on the expansion of financial inclusion and digital retail payments. The insights gained from these research endeavors will inform IPAs efforts in promoting financial inclusion in Tanzania. The concrete results from these initiatives will be reported in coming annual reports
In addition, and importantly according to Sida, IPA seeks to enhance access to funding for local researchers. In order to achieve this goal, IPA held workshops that provided tailored proposal development and support to local researchers, as well as matchmaking opportunities to capitalize on diverse perspectives and local knowledge when forming teams. These workshops led to the submission of 37 proposals for new research projects, with 13 projects led by a local researcher successfully awarded funding. IPA further aims to develop a pipeline of researchers through research activities conducted in the IPA country offices globally. For instance, to offer early career researchers a chance to gain hands on experience, IPA established the African Internship Program across all country offices.
In 2023, IPA identified 11 impact cases, where IPAs evidence translated into sizeable impacts. The best bet report was published which focuses on the most promising emerging innovations that have the greatest potential to scale. https://poverty-action.org/sites/default/files/2023-11/IPA-Best-Bets-Report-Updated.pdf They have identified 50 such cases, divided into three categories; emerging, exploratory and established, for each case they describe the problem, overview of the evidence, cost and whats needed. For example: Becoming One: Couples counseling to reduce intimate partner violence in Uganda, and now scaling up of becoming one to 10000 Ugandans couples to reduce intimate partner violence.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
